description:
## Problem

Reach uses EEx.Engine for HEEx template processing. EEx.eval_string/2 evaluates arbitrary Elixir code from strings — this is a code execution vector. Also missing: IO.write/IO.puts with tainted data (output sinks for data exfiltration).

## Evidence

From reach:
- reach/lib/reach/plugins/live_view/heex_engine.ex: @behaviour EEx.Engine
- reach/lib/reach/plugins/live_view/heex/parser.ex: EEx.SyntaxError handling

From ex_dna:
- ex_dna/lib/ex_dna/reporter/console.ex: IO.puts for output

## Expected Behavior

- EEx.eval_string should be flagged as CodeExecution
- EEx.eval_file should be flagged as CodeExecution
- IO.write/IO.puts with tainted data should be flagged as data exfiltration

## Suggested Fix

Add to rules/elixir-sinks.kdl:
- sink "EEx.eval_string" arg=0 { fix "Avoid evaluating user input as EEx templates" }
- sink "EEx.eval_file" arg=0 { fix "Avoid evaluating user-controlled files as EEx templates" }

IO.write/IO.puts are lower priority — they're output sinks, not security sinks.
title: Elixir: add EEx.eval_string and IO.write as security sinks
